sample_unit: de-identified JIA use cases (rated by 3 rheumatologists); patient evaluation n=34

links.outcome: Rheumatologist-rated acceptability of LLM decision aid outputs: safety, factual consistency, appropriateness, preference acknowledgment
links.effect: 97% acceptable for safety and preference acknowledgment, 60% for factual consistency, 70% for appropriateness; inter-rater agreement poor for factual consistency.
links.quote: Rheumatologists rated 97% of outputs as acceptable for safety and preference acknowledgment, 60% for factual consistency, 70% for appropriateness.

unlisted_practices: LLM-as-a-Judge exploratory evaluation of LLM outputs
LLM-based decision aid to support shared/collaborative decision-making with patients
qualitative patient perspective evaluation of decision aid

screen.reason: Multimethod feasibility study evaluating an LLM-based decision aid for juvenile idiopathic arthritis using clinical vignettes evaluated by rheumatologists, an LLM judge, and patient feedback.
